# Built skills

### accounting

| Skill | Title | Description | Scopes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `map-gl-accounts` | Map GL Accounts to the Chart of Accounts | Map SKU.io's accounting roles (sales, shipping revenue, COGS, inventory control, purchase clearing, accounts receivable, accounts payable, sales tax, and the optional ones) to the customer's own chart of accounts — the QuickBooks Online or Xero accounts that SKU.io holds as nominal codes. Reads the current mapping and the available accounts, proposes a full mapping table with the reasoning for each choice, waits for the user's explicit approval (ideally their bookkeeper's), then saves only the approved keys and reports what changed. Use it for the Launch Roadmap's "Map GL accounts" step or whenever journals fail for a missing nominal code mapping. Finance-sensitive: a wrong mapping posts every future journal to the wrong account. | accounting:read, settings:read, settings:write |
| `reconcile-supplier-statement` | Reconcile a Supplier Statement | Reconcile what a supplier says you owe them against SKU.io's accounts payable, and trace the bank payments in between. Takes the supplier's statement (an emailed QuickBooks/Xero statement, a PDF, or pasted text) plus the bank lines paid to that supplier, compares them with the supplier's bills, vendor credits and payments in SKU.io, and explains every difference: bills a payment settled but SKU.io still shows open, payments recorded twice, credits applied in SKU.io that the supplier has not applied, bill totals that differ from the supplier's invoice (missing freight, a mis-linked line), and documents one side has that the other lacks. Proposes the fix for each and, under the caller's approval policy, applies the SKU.io side: unapply or apply credits, record a supplier payment, remove a duplicate payment. Use for "does our statement from X match", "why does SKU.io say we owe X more than they do", or a regular supplier account reconciliation. | suppliers:read, purchase-orders:read, purchase-orders:write, accounting:read, accounting:write, settings:read |
| `record-vendor-credit` | Record a Vendor Credit | Record a supplier's credit memo (vendor credit, credit note) in SKU.io from the memo document — a PDF or email from the supplier — then apply it to the supplier bill(s) it should reduce. Built for non-inventory credits: co-op or advertising credits, marketing allowances, rebates paid as account credit, overbilling and other "only what we owe changes" credits. Checks for a duplicate by credit number, follows how the account recorded earlier credits from the same supplier (date, expense account, wording), creates the credit as a draft, previews its accounting impact, authorizes it, allocates it to an open purchase invoice, attaches the source document, and prints direct links. Returned or damaged goods and price corrections against a PO line are flagged and routed rather than forced into a financial-only credit. | accounting:read, accounting:write, purchase-orders:read, suppliers:read, settings:read |

### integrations

| Skill | Title | Description | Scopes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `manage-amazon-recovery` | Manage Amazon Recovery Cases | Work Amazon FBA reimbursement claims end to end from SKU.io's Amazon Recovery: triage cases SKU.io found (confirm against the evidence or dismiss), file ready cases with Amazon using the filing pack SKU.io prepares (case text, the details Amazon asks for, files to attach, grouped shipment and product filings), record the Amazon case ID, and follow up on filed cases by recording Amazon's answer and sending the reply or appeal. Use it when asked to file, chase, or clean up Amazon reimbursement claims, lost/damaged inventory, inbound shortages, or FBA fee overcharges. Filing itself happens in Amazon Seller Central, which the calling agent operates; this skill says what to do there and records every outcome back in SKU.io. | recovery:read, recovery:write |
| `optimize-tiktok-listing-quality` | Optimize TikTok Shop Listing Quality | Lift a TikTok Shop integration's listings out of POOR/FAIR Listing Quality toward GOOD, driven by TikTok's own "Diagnose and Optimize Product" results. For each in-scope listing it reads the cached diagnosis (re-diagnosing first when stale or missing), then for every issue TikTok reports — keyed on the field (TITLE / DESCRIPTION / IMAGE), its `code`, `how_to_solve` guidance and the suggested `seo_words` — plans a concrete fix: a rewritten title, an expanded description, and a sourced replacement image (images are never auto-generated). It runs POOR before FAIR, defaults to a dry-run that emits the proposed copy as a diff for approval, and — on the built apply endpoint (`POST .../products/{product}/optimize`, with AI-drafted copy from `.../optimize/draft`) — writes the approved title/description/main-image back to the live listing and re-diagnoses to confirm the tier improved. Use it for "fix our TikTok listing quality", "get these POOR listings to GOOD", or "why are these listings rated FAIR". | integrations:read, integrations:write |

### inventory

| Skill | Title | Description | Scopes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `adjust-inventory` | Adjust Inventory | Adjust the on-hand quantity of a product at a warehouse in SKU.io — an increase, a decrease, or a set-to-value. Use this for stock takes, corrections, damage/shrinkage write-offs, or found stock. Resolve the product with find-product first so the adjustment targets the right product and warehouse. | inventory:write, products:read |
| `set-initial-inventory` | Set Initial Inventory | Load opening stock into SKU.io as an initial (first-ever) count for one or more warehouses, dated to the account's inventory start date. Use this when going live, onboarding a new warehouse or 3PL, or importing an opening count sheet: it settles the start date (from the source data or by asking — the configured setting is often stale, so confirm it), turns the sheet into one initial stock take per warehouse, and drives each draft → open → closed so the quantities and their cost layers land. It also attaches the source documents to the take, files the rows it could not resolve cleanly — unmapped SKUs, lines with no cost basis, damaged stock nobody split out, sheets declared incomplete — as an HTML anomaly report, and works those anomalies once answers come back: creating missing products, updating lines, posting a revised report. An initial count happens once per warehouse and cannot be re-dated, so date and unit costs must be right before finalizing. For cycle counts or corrections use adjust-inventory. | inventory:read, inventory:write, warehouses:read, settings:write, products:read |

### manufacturing

| Skill | Title | Description | Scopes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `build-boms` | Build Bills of Materials from a Recipe Sheet | Create bills of materials (BOMs, recipes) in SKU.io for manufactured products from a recipe sheet the user already keeps — a spreadsheet or file in their Drive or email listing each finished product's ingredients or parts and quantities. Finds manufactured products with no BOM, maps the sheet's rows to products and units of measure, proposes each BOM for approval, creates them as drafts in batches of at most 25, and reports what changed. Use it for the Launch Roadmap's "Bills of materials" step, when onboarding a manufacturer, or whenever a manufactured product has no recipe. It never edits, archives or deletes an existing BOM. | products:read, manufacturing:read, manufacturing:write |

### platform

| Skill | Title | Description | Scopes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `connect-to-sku` | Connect to SKU.io | The entry point for any SKU.io task. Establish an authenticated connection: point at the correct tenant base URL, send a Personal Access Token as a Bearer token, and prove it works with GET /api/me — the scope-free identity call whose tenant_id confirms you are on the account the user meant and whose token.scopes tell you what the token may do, so you can check for a missing scope up front instead of hitting a 403 mid-operation. Use this first whenever you are about to call the SKU.io API. | settings:read, warehouses:read |
| `create-saved-view` | Create a Saved View (and favorite it) | Create a saved view for any SKU.io data table (products, sales orders, inventory, …) — a named, reusable configuration of visible columns, filters, sort, and search — and favorite it so it appears on the table's favorites bar. Use this to give a user a one-click way back to a specific slice of data: a fresh import, an exception queue, a curated report. Composable — other skills (e.g. build-product-catalog) call it to leave behind a view of what they just created. | settings:write |
| `create-workflow` | Create a Workflow (automation) | Build, validate, publish, test-run and maintain SKU.io automation workflows from the API — the same node/edge graph the visual Workflow Builder draws. Use this whenever a user wants something to happen automatically in response to something else: email or Slack me when an order lands on a given sales channel, tag or note orders that match a rule, post a webhook to another system, import a supplier feed from FTP on a schedule, or route orders to a warehouse — and when an existing workflow needs changing, pausing, or diagnosing because it did not fire. Starts from a template when one fits, discovers the node catalog and credentials live, and publishes only after a dry run the user has seen — including picking the right moment to fire on, which for an order alert is the channel import rather than the sales-order creation. | settings:read, settings:write |
| `follow-launch-roadmap` | Follow the Launch Roadmap | Work through an account's SKU.io Launch Roadmap with the user: read their launch plan, pick the steps that are theirs and unblocked, explain each one (what it is, why it matters, how SKU.io will know it's done), hand off to the matching skill to do the work together — catalog import, bundles, BOMs, supplier costs, opening stock, GL mapping and more — then post a progress comment on the step and re-check it. Use it when the user asks "what's next on our launch?", "help me with my onboarding steps", or names a roadmap step. SKU.io's own data checks decide when a step is done; this skill never signs off checkpoints or unblocks steps (people do that in the app), ticks a manual step only when the user confirms it, and marks a stuck step blocked with the reason. | launch_plan:read, launch_plan:write |
| `sync-sops` | Sync your SOPs with SKU.io changes | Keep your internal Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) in step with SKU.io. SKU.io ships often — menus move, workflows change, features are added — which quietly breaks the step-by-step procedures your team relies on. Give this skill your SOP content plus the date you last reviewed it: it reads SKU.io's public changelog and documentation, finds the changes that affect your procedures, and rewrites the exact stale steps — or drafts a brand-new SOP from the current docs, in your own format. Use it whenever internal docs/SOPs may be out of date, or on a schedule to catch drift. | settings:read |

### products

| Skill | Title | Description | Scopes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `build-product-catalog` | Build a Product Catalog from Any Source | Turn product information from any source — a spreadsheet or CSV, a Google Sheet, a supplier price list, a website or product page, or pasted text — into products in SKU.io. Extract the raw rows, map them onto SKU.io's product fields, de-duplicate against the existing catalog, then create the products. Use this to onboard a new catalog, import a supplier's range, or bulk-load products from an external system. | products:write, products:read |
| `configure-bundles` | Configure Bundles and Kits | Give every bundle and kit in SKU.io its components. Finds bundle/kit products that have no components yet (and standard products whose names look like packs or sets), proposes each recipe from a component list the user supplies (a sheet or file in their Drive or email) or from its channel listing titles, gets the user's approval, then saves the components in batches of at most 25 and reports what changed. Use it for the Launch Roadmap's "Configure kits & bundles" step, after importing channel listings that turned out to be multi-packs or sets, or whenever the Product Data Health report shows kits or bundles without components. It never replaces a recipe that already has components and never deletes anything. | products:read, products:write |
| `enrich-channel-content` | Enrich Product Content for a Sales Channel | Fill in the channel-specific product content a marketplace needs before you can list there — today, a per-channel description attribute such as tiktokshop_description — supplier by supplier or brand by brand. For each product it gathers what already exists (the live Amazon or eBay copy, the product's own attributes), asks SKU.io's AI to amalgamate it into copy that follows the target channel's own rules, and renders an HTML review report — product image, every source side by side, the proposal, and the AI's rationale — with approve/reject per product. Only approved descriptions are written back. When no copy exists anywhere it falls back to the manufacturer's site, and finally to a drafted email asking the supplier. Use it whenever "we can't list these on TikTok Shop / Walmart / Temu because the descriptions are missing" — or whenever a channel's content rules differ enough that reusing another channel's description would be wrong. | products:read, products:write, suppliers:read |
| `find-matrix-opportunities` | Find Matrix (Variant) Product Opportunities | Scan a SKU.io catalog for groups of standalone products that are really one product in several sizes, colours, or styles, and should be a matrix (variant) family instead of separate flat SKUs. Clusters the catalog by name and SKU pattern, corroborates each candidate against the seller's Amazon listings when an Amazon integration exists — Amazon's own variation relationships and per-child colour/size values are the strongest available evidence — ranks the candidates by sales and data readiness, then optionally builds the matrix parents and attaches the children. Use this when someone asks which products should be grouped as variants, wants variation/swatch listings for a marketplace, or asks why their size/colour products are listed one by one. | products:read, products:write, integrations:read |
| `find-product` | Find a Product | Look up a product in the SKU.io catalog by SKU, barcode, or a free-text search over name and SKU. Use this whenever you need to resolve a product reference to its SKU.io product record and id — for example before adding it to a sales order, checking stock, or reporting on it. | products:read |
| `map-supplier-costs` | Map Supplier Costs onto Reorderable Products | Fill in what the business pays its suppliers for every product it reorders, until at least 95% of active reorderable products (standard, kit, manufactured, blemished) carry a non-zero supplier price. Finds the products with no supplier pricing, sources each cost from the user's supplier price lists (files in their Drive or email) or, failing that, from the last price paid on a past purchase order, proposes a cost table for approval, then writes the supplier tier prices in batches of at most 25 and reports what changed. Use it for the Launch Roadmap's "Supplier costs" step or when the Product Data Health report shows products without supplier pricing. It fills gaps; it never unlinks suppliers or deletes prices. To apply a supplier's new price file to products that already have costs, use update-catalog-pricing. | products:read, products:write, suppliers:read, purchase-orders:read |
| `publish-listing` | Publish or Update a Channel Listing | List a product on a sales channel — Amazon, eBay, Walmart, Shopify, BigCommerce, WooCommerce, TikTok Shop, Temu, Faire — or revise a listing that is already live. Drives SKU.io's listing-draft workflow end to end: read per-channel publish readiness, pick the channel category (on Amazon, the product type), map the channel's required fields from product data, validate against the channel's own schema, then publish and follow the attempt log. Use this whenever someone wants a product listed, re-listed, scheduled, or its listing content updated on a marketplace or storefront. | products:read, products:write |
| `update-catalog-pricing` | Update Catalog Pricing from a Price File | Apply a new price file to products that already exist in SKU.io — a supplier's updated wholesale/cost list, a new MSRP sheet, or any repriced list. Match each row to an existing product (SKU, supplier SKU, MPN, or barcode), diff old vs new prices, get the user's confirmation, then update supplier pricing tiers (what you pay) and/or product pricing tiers (what you charge). Use this when a supplier sends "new pricing effective <date>" or the business reprices a range; it never creates products (that is build-product-catalog). | products:read, products:write, suppliers:read |

### purchase-orders

| Skill | Title | Description | Scopes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `create-purchase-order` | Create a Purchase Order | Create a purchase order in SKU.io — a replenishment order placed with a supplier — from either a plain description of what to buy or a source document (a supplier email, an order-form spreadsheet, a demand-plan export) that supplies the SKUs and quantities. Resolves the supplier, destination warehouse, unit costs, currency, and (optionally) payment term, builds the line items, and creates the PO as a draft or an open order. Covers standard and consignment replenishment. Resolve products with find-product first so every line references a real product. | purchase-orders:write, suppliers:read, warehouses:read, products:read, settings:read |
| `record-purchase-invoice` | Record a Purchase Invoice | Record a supplier's invoice (a bill / accounts-payable invoice) against a purchase order in SKU.io, from the invoice document itself — a PDF or email from the supplier — or from a plain description. Handles multi-invoice PDFs (a scanned batch of several invoices in one file) by recording each invoice separately and attaching only its own pages. Resolves the PO, maps the invoice's line items to PO lines and its freight/fee charges to the PO's financial lines, checks for duplicates by supplier invoice number, creates the purchase invoice, attaches the source document, and verifies the result with a three-way match. Also corrects an existing bill that differs from the supplier's invoice: a mis-linked line, a missing freight line, a wrong fee quantity, number or date. Ends by printing a direct link to every invoice recorded. Can also record a payment against the invoice once one has actually been made. | purchase-orders:read, purchase-orders:write, settings:read |

### settings

| Skill | Title | Description | Scopes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `edit-packing-slip-template` | Edit a Packing-Slip PDF Template | Edit a SKU.io packing-slip PDF template with the packing-specific rules that keep the footer banner, logo, and per-store layouts consistent. Use this when changing a packing slip's footer banner or branding, or when the banner renders inconsistently — present on some orders or stores, missing or clipped on others. Enforces the exact footer-banner structure the PDF export requires to pin a banner to every page, the banner aspect ratio, cross-store consistency, and a multi-order visual QA pass against real orders. Extends edit-pdf-template — do the base edit/validate/save loop there; this adds the packing rules. | settings:read, settings:write |
| `edit-pdf-template` | Edit a PDF Template | Edit any SKU.io PDF document template — packing slips, quotes, sales orders, pick lists, purchase orders, and vendor/sales credits — by editing its HTML content directly, then validating, previewing against real and mock documents, and visually QA-ing the rendered PDF before saving. Use this to change branding, layout, a logo or footer banner, or which fields a document shows. Runs a deterministic read → edit → validate → preview → verify → save loop; every save snapshots a version you can restore, so edits are reversible. Prefer this over the in-app AI builder, which is the fallback for users without an agent. For packing slips, load edit-packing-slip-template too. | settings:read, settings:write |
